title: FDA approves drug to treat infant-onset Niemann-Pick Type C | News | News & Media | College of Science | University of Notre Dame
summary:
The Ara Parseghian Medical Research Fund (APMRF) at the University of Notre Dame joins families affected by Niemann-Pick Type C (NPC) disease in celebrating the first U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of a medication proven to improve survival in infantile-onset NPC.

...

The FDA approved LEMBAZ™ (2-hydroxypropyl-beta- cyclodextrin, adrabetadex) on November 17, 2026. It has been shown to reduce the risk of death in adults and children whose NPC neurological symptoms began before age 6.

title: Gene therapy for blindness moves closer to patients
summary:
Some people who had lost almost all their sight to an inherited eye disease could find objects on a table again after a single gene injection and training with special goggles.

None could read or recognise a face, but before treatment, the best any of them could see was a hand moving in front of the eye. 

The results come from a small trial recently published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

summary:

summary:
